intro: What the federal funds rate is, who sets its target range, how decisions are announced, and what the rate can affect in the wider economy.
explanation:
## What the federal funds rate is

The federal funds rate is the price of an overnight loan from one depository institution to another, made out of balances held at the Federal Reserve. The Federal Reserve does not announce one number. It announces a target range, and the rate that banks actually pay is meant to stay inside it.

## Who sets the target range

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets it. There are twelve votes. Governors on the Board hold seven of them and the New York Reserve Bank's president holds one. The other four go to Reserve Bank presidents from the remaining eleven banks, chosen in rotation for one-year terms. Those who are not voting still attend the meetings and add to the discussion.

Eight meetings are scheduled each year, and extra ones can be called when needed. The Fed says its decisions support its dual mandate. After each meeting the Committee issues a statement, and an implementation note gives the date any change takes effect. For regularly scheduled meetings, the minutes come out three weeks after the decision. The Fed publishes the meeting calendar on its own site.

## How the Fed steers the rate

Reserve requirements and the discount rate sit with the Board of Governors, while open market operations belong to the FOMC. Together these are the Fed's policy instruments. Between them, they shape how much banks want, and how much is available, of the balances held at the Reserve Banks, and that shifts the federal funds rate. The Board also sets the interest rate paid on those reserve balances, which the Fed describes as an important tool for carrying out its policy.

## What the rate can affect

A change in the rate sets off a series of effects, the Fed says: other short-term and long-term interest rates move, exchange rates are affected, and so is the supply of money and credit. Later effects can reach employment, output, and prices.
